correctness.rationale: A pure-product decomposition gives the exact factorization M=[x T]=sum p_k a_k(1,b_k^T), with every rank-one summand of nuclear norm sqrt(2), hence ||M||_*<=sqrt(2). If s1>=s2>=s3 are the singular values, the standard geometric-discord formula is D=(s2^2+s3^2)/2. From s1+s2+s3<=sqrt(2), ordering gives 2s2+s3<=sqrt(2) and 0<=s3<=sqrt(2)/3; the resulting one-variable quadratic is at most 1/2, hence D<=1/4. Equality forces (s1,s2,s3)=(1/sqrt(2),1/sqrt(2),0). A polar partial-isometry norming functional forces every augmented Bloch vector c_k=(1,b_k) into its two-dimensional initial space; intersecting that plane with c_0=1 and ||c||=sqrt(2) gives at most two points, so rank(rho)<=2. The prior rank-two classification then yields the unique local-unitary orbit. The exact checker confirms the extremizer and scalar algebra; no finite experiment carries the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This settles a published 2012 conjecture for the complete separable two-qubit state space, not a finite table or arbitrary slice. It gives both the sharp value and the complete equality class and exposes a compact convex-geometric mechanism through the augmented Bloch nuclear norm. The result meaningfully extends the known rank-two and X-state cases.
